newsitem.title: USA: NHL ICE HOCKEY-HASEK PRACTICES FOR FIRST TIME SINCE INJURY, ALTERCATION.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY-HASEK PRACTICES FOR FIRST TIME SINCE INJURY, ALTERCATION.

text.p: Buffalo goaltender Dominik Hasek, who was suspended for the first three games of the Sabres' upcoming playoff series with Philadelphia, practiced Friday for the first time since injuring his knee in the first round of the playoffs.
Hasek also addressed the media for the first time since the physical confrontation with a Buffalo sportsat led to his suspension.

Hasek has since appologized to Buffalo News sportswriter Jim Kelley, who enraged the star goaltender by questioning in his column the severity of the injury and Hasek's desire to return to the Sabres' net after suffering a sprained knee in Game 3 of the opening-round series with Ottawa.
"My actions were wrong and what I did was not acceptable," Hasek said of the incident.

Hasek ran into Kelley in the arena hallway following Game 5 of the Ottawa series and grabbed the reporter's shirtcollar with both hands. The two were separated, but not before angry words were exchanged and Hasek ripped the Kelley's shirt.
"Kids cannot respond like that. It's not acceptable no matter what someone says about you," a contrite Hasek told reporters. "Everything was unfortunate and I feel really bad about it."

Sabres backup netminder Steve Shields, who helped Buffalo survive a tough seven-game series with the Senators, will start at least the first three games of the Eastern Conference semifinal with the Philadelphia Flyers, which begins Saturday.
Shields compiled a .939 save percentage with a 1.80 goals-against average in the four-plus playoff games in relief of Hasek.

"I want to say right now I'm very glad everything is over," Hasek said following Friday's practice. "Now I can concentrate just on playing hockey, 100 percent on beating the Philadelphia Flyers. That's most important right now."
Hasek, who led Buffalo to a division title this season, is widely expected to be one of the finalists for the Hart Trophy, which goes to the league's Most Valuable Player.
Despite being sidelined for two weeks with a hairline rib fracture, Hasek posted 37 wins and a league-high .930 save percentage.
